prompt:
Extract the one contact block from the note: contact label/value lines in any order, with label variants and colon, equals, or tab separators. Ignore all other text. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country"; all values are strings or null.

Trim values and collapse whitespace runs. Absent, blank, and whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD; any case) are missing. Assign email by @ and phone by content: after dropping a leading tel: and trailing ext., ext, x, #, or extension plus extension digits, the remainder must use only digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . /, with at least seven digits. Do not rely on email/phone labels. Take country from its own line. Take name and company from their labels, swapping them if the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not.

• Name: Move the part after the first comma before the part preceding it for Last, First. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (optional dot, any case). Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate.
• Company: Remove one trailing legal suffix plus an optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Trim, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
• Email: Strip mailto: and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.
• Country line: Convert English, Swedish, or German country names or alpha-2/alpha-3 codes, in any case, to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Aliases: UK/Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA/U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
• Phone: After removing tel: and extensions, check for leading + or 00, ignoring a leading opening parenthesis. If international, convert 00 to +, remove (0) and all formatting separators (spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, parentheses), and keep the written calling code regardless of the country line. Otherwise strip formatting separators, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code, or return null if no country. The result is E.164: + and digits only, including the calling code.

Missing fields are null, with exactly one exception: if country is missing and the phone is international, use the country of its calling code only if unique. Shared codes such as +1 and +7 yield null. Never fill fields from notes, signatures, domains, company suffixes, or guesses.
